answers.how: The boat’s image position stays nearly fixed while its distance decreases by 4.0505 m between 1 s and 2 s; the full-clip scaling change is consistent with this speed.
At 1 s, the boat is about 272 px tall including its mast, versus about 49 px for the person. Applying the supplied depth correction gives 1.75 × (272/49) × (96.8995/92.1861).
The boat’s full horizontal extent is about 103 px at 1 s. Scaling against the 49 px person and correcting for their different distances gives about 3.88 m.
The person moves approximately 113 px over 2.958 s. Using the 1.75 m height over approximately 49 px gives the average speed.
Spread-wing frames show a depth-corrected tip-to-tip extent equivalent to approximately 51.5 px at the person’s distance. Multiplying by 1.75/49 gives the wingspan.
Combined the eagle’s approximately 11.74 m/s depth change with its depth-corrected transverse motion, measured across the frames.
